the development and application of new technologies for the detection of foodborne pathogens.

the SimPlate colorm and E. coli CEc-CI color indicator method and the AOAC 966.23 and AOAC 96624 reference methods are equivalent for enumerating and presumptively confirming total coliforms in food products and for enumerating and confirmatively detecting E. coli in food products.
the SimPlate method for total coliforms is equivalent to the reference culture method and the SimPlate method and the reference method are equivalent for E. coli in all foods tested.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SimPlate method was found to be equivalent to the AOAC methods for enumerating total coliforms in foods.
the SimPlate method is a reliable and accurate alternative to the AOAC culture methods for enumeration of both coliform bacteria and Escherichian coli in foods.
the SimPlate method is a viable alternative to the AOAC culture reference methods for enumerating coliforms and/or E. coli in a wide variety of foods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SimPlate system can be a valuable tool for enumerating coliforms and/or E. coli in food products, especially in situations when a large number of samples must be tested.
the SimPlate system can be used as an alternative to the 3-tube most probable number (MPN) method for enumeration of total coliform bacteria and Escherichi a coli in foods.
the SimPlate method is an alternative, reliable and rapid method to culture-based methods for the determination of coliform and E.coli levels.
